majority_rule.tie_rule: In a 50-50 Senate the Vice President, as President of the Senate, casts tie-breaking votes; the current Vice President is JD Vance (R). Control therefore requires 51 seats, or 50 seats plus the vice presidency.
majority_rule.constitutional_basis: U.S. Constitution, Article I, Section 3: the Vice President "shall be President of the Senate, but shall have no Vote, unless they be equally divided."
majority_rule.arithmetic: Republicans hold 53 seats. If the Vice President breaks ties for Republicans, Democrats (with the 2 independents) need a net gain of 4 seats to reach 51.

notes_uncertain: Generic-ballot and approval poll lists come from NBC News source-poll tables (index only; its averages are excluded). Polls the index did not list may be missing. Undecided shares are not given by the index.
NBC index URL for the ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos LV row ends in 'October-2027' (likely a typo in the index); the RV row's URL ends in 'October-2026'.
partisan_sponsor = 'none' follows the NBC index flag isPartisanAffiliated (false for every row in the period); no independent check of each sponsor's affiliation was made.
pollster/sponsor split is mechanical from the listed poll name (last segment = pollster, except known joint pollster pairs); 'poll_name_as_listed' keeps the original.
Several polls were in the field in late August/September and ended on or after Sept 1; field_end is used as the inclusion date (publication dates were not checked one by one).

CA-1 special election: Wikipedia gives the 2024 presidential result only for the newly redrawn (Proposition 50) district (Harris 54.5-42.3); the presidential result for the lines used in the special election was not found.
Wyoming 2020 seat result: Wikipedia race-summary table says 72.9%, state section text says 72.8% (Cynthia Lummis).
UCSB lists 20 Senate seats to defend for the president's party in 2026 (apparently Class 2 only); the ballot has 22 Republican-held seats including the FL and OH specials.
GA-14 and NJ-11 specials: the district-level 2024 presidential result was not collected.
Reuters/Ipsos releases report more than one generic-ballot version (e.g., with and without leaners); the index values are used as listed and were not re-checked against each release.
senate.gov returned HTTP 403; current Senate composition is taken from Wikipedia's 119th Congress party summary (with dated changes) and matches the 2026 Senate elections infobox (53 R, 45 D, 2 I).
